study_sample_descriptor.occupation_type: Skilled Digital Freelancers (Accountants and Software Engineers via Upwork)

boundary_spanning_measures.source_quote: [Methodology, p. 51-52] "Ancona et al. (1992A) developed a boundary spanning scale that aids in understanding boundary spanning at a micro level. The six scouting items from this scale were used for this study because they measure high-frequency communicators, expertise, and access to information, which are characteristics of skilled digital freelancers." Scouting sub-dimension only. Items adapted: network wording substituted for competing organization wording due to non-disclosure concerns. 5-point Likert from Strongly Disagree (1) to Strongly Agree (5). In-text alpha = 0.858; Table 3 (p. 119) renders 0.859.

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: Original 10-item scale; 1 item removed to increase alpha from 0.691 to 0.707, yielding 9 final items.
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Methodology, pp. 48-49] "interaction was measured using an established interdependence scale (Pearce et al., 1991) due to its reliability and validity of measuring employee-perceived, self-report task interdependence."

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: Original 4-item scale augmented with 2 additional items after pilot study to increase alpha from 0.745 to 0.800.
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Methodology, pp. 49-50] "The 4-item Hinkin et al. (1989) expert power scale was adapted from the seminal work of French et al. (1959)."

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: Ordinal college education level (1 = low [no education/associate], 2 = medium [bachelor's], 3 = high [master's/PhD]); Table 1 M = 2.314, SD = 0.610.
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Results, p. 66] "Skilled digital freelancer level of college education was used to measure human capital. Low level of education = 1 and included no education or an associate degree; medium level of education = 2 and included a bachelor’s degree; and high level of education = 3 and included a master’s degree or PhD."

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: Table 1 (p. 117) omits Mean and SD for Referent Power (coded 999 per Rule 1); Cronbach's alpha = 0.897 from Table 3 (p. 119).
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Methodology, p. 50] "Specifically, the 4-item referent power scale (Hinkin & Schriesheim, 1989) was applied as a post hoc test."

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: Collaborate 6-item subscale with 1 item removed to yield 5 final items (Table 3, p. 119 alpha = 0.825).
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Methodology, p. 50] "Collaboration was assessed using an established strategic orientation toward brokering scale (Soda et al., 2018)."

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: 3-item blue attitude marker variable included in Table 2 (7. Marker Variable); Mean, SD, and alpha not reported in Tables 1 or 3 (coded 999 per Rule 1).
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Appendix F: Survey Instrument, p. 113] "MARKER VARIABLES (Miller & Simmering, 2022) Likert Scale: 1 = Strongly Disagree; 2 = Disagree; 3 = Neutral; 4 = Agree; 5 = Strongly Agree. I think blue is a pretty color. I like the color blue. Blue is a lovely color."

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: 47% female (n = 66) and 53% male (n = 77); Mean and SD not reported in Table 1.
non_bs_measures.specific_measure_used: The gender you identify with is
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Appendix F: Survey Instrument, p. 114] "2.) The gender you identify with is: a. Male b. Female c. Non-binary/third gender d. Prefer not to say" [Sample, p. 61] "Forty seven percent of participants identified as female (n = 66) and 53% as male (n = 77)."

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: Self-reported Upwork reputation rating item; Mean and SD omitted in Table 1 (coded 999 per Rule 1).
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Appendix F: Survey Instrument, p. 114] "4.) What is your reputation rating?"

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: 5 ordinal categories from 0% (1) to 100% (5) weekly remote freelance work; Table 1 M = 4.279, SD = 1.460.
non_bs_measures.specific_measure_used: percentage of your weekly freelance work is typically conducted remotely
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Appendix F: Survey Instrument, p. 114] "7.) What percentage of your weekly freelance work is typically conducted remotely (rather than at the employing organization's site)? a. 0% b. Up to 25% c. Up to 50% d. Up to 75% e. 100%"

non_bs_measures.report_type_note: Recoded into 3 ordinal duration categories (<6 months = 1, 6-12 months = 2, >1 year = 3); Table 1 M = 1.489, SD = 0.812.
non_bs_measures.specific_measure_used: contract times of less than 6 months = 1, 6 – 12 months = 2, and greater than 1 year = 3
non_bs_measures.source_quote: [Results, p. 68] "I analyzed contract time by contrasting contract times of less than 6 months = 1, 6 – 12 months = 2, and greater than 1 year = 3."
